purpose: Targeted small-native-duplex availability check during serialized text training; no weights downloaded.

models.name: LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B
models.observed: Official card describes1.5B end-to-end speech/text model,1.2B language backbone,115M FastConformer encoder and interleaved output. Repository supplies fine-tuning interfaces. Its multi-turn example completes the user audio turn before calling interleaved generation.
models.inference: Small trainable speech model is potentially relevant, but this evidence does not establish concurrent listening during generated speech or semantic interruption handling. Interleaved text/audio output alone does not prove full duplex.
models.decision: No substitution or download for the current native full-duplex requirement.

models.name: BayLing-Duplex
models.observed: Paper describes a9B GLM-4-Voice backbone with user audio, generated text and generated audio channels plus dialogue-state tokens; modified Whisper-large-v3 tokenizer and flow-matching speech decoder.
models.inference: This is not a smaller drop-in native backbone for the8GBMac. It requires a different training/runtime/codec implementation.
models.decision: Keep as a methodological reference, not a download or measured local benchmark.

models.name: NemotronLabs VoiceChat
models.observed: Paper uses Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2-Base,600M streaming FastConformer, and977M speech generation including codec. Parallel text/function output and continuous speech decoder are documented.
models.inference: Larger aggregate model than the current Moshi path; the paper does not establish an8GBApple inference or training solution.
models.decision: No large download. Reported benchmark gains are not local performance evidence.

result: No verified smaller native full-duplex replacement identified in these three primary-source checks. This is not an exhaustive impossibility claim. Current run26 and matched native control remain the next experiments.
